chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Habeeb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, and with the seller were two slaves. So he said to the buyer, 'Go with both of them and choose whichever you wish, and return the other,' and he had taken the money. So the buyer went with both of them, and one of them absconded from his presence.

He said: Let him return the one who is still with him and take back half the price from what he gave to the seller, and go in search of the slave. If he finds him, he can choose whichever of the two he wishes and return the half money which he had taken; and if he does not find him, the slave is shared between them, half for the seller and half for the buyer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one of two slaves sold together absconds before the buyer chooses?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *Khiyar al-Majlis* (option of the meeting) in a conditional sale, ruling that the buyer must return the remaining slave and reclaim half the price to pursue the missing one. If the absconded slave is not recovered, the remaining slave becomes a joint property (*Musha*) between seller and buyer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of preserving equity when the specific object of sale is uncertain. This ruling underscores the importance of clear ownership division in cases of partial performance and loss within commercial contracts.
